questions.title: Diagonal sum
questions.statement: Read an n×n matrix and print the sum of its main diagonal.

examples.explain: m[i][i] for every row is the main diagonal.

mistakes: Summing the anti-diagonal as well
hints: Compare the row and column index.

questions.title: Factorial with recursion
questions.statement: Read n and print n! using a recursive method.

examples.explain: factorial(n) = n * factorial(n-1), with 0! = 1.

mistakes: Missing the base case, causing a StackOverflowError
hints: 0! and 1! are both 1.

questions.title: Recursive Fibonacci
questions.statement: Print the n-th Fibonacci number (0-based: F0=0, F1=1) using recursion.

examples.explain: fib(n) = fib(n-1) + fib(n-2).

mistakes: Returning 1 for n=0
hints: Two base cases: 0 and 1.

questions.title: Binary to decimal
questions.statement: Read a binary string and print its decimal value.

examples.explain: Result = result*2 + digit for every bit.

mistakes: Using Integer.parseInt(bits, 2) on a long input and overflowing
hints: Horner's method: shift left and add the bit.

questions.title: Decimal to binary
questions.statement: Read a non-negative integer and print its binary representation without using built-in conversion helpers.
questions.output: Binary digits with no leading zeros (0 for zero).

examples.explain: Repeatedly take n%2 and prepend it while n shrinks.

mistakes: Forgetting the special case for 0, which prints an empty string
hints: Reverse the collected remainders at the end.

questions.title: Stack implementation
questions.statement: Implement a stack supporting push, pop, peek and size. Read commands until end and print the result of pop, peek and size.
questions.input: Commands: push X, pop, peek, size, end.
questions.output: One line per command that returns a value.
constraints: Only valid commands; never pop or peek an empty stack.

examples.input:
push 5
push 3
pop
peek
size
end
examples.explain: pop removes and prints 3, peek shows 5, size is 1.

tests.name: mixed commands
tests.input:
push 5
push 3
pop
peek
size
end

mistakes: Using Stack (legacy, synchronized) instead of ArrayDeque
hints: ArrayDeque push/pop act on the head.

questions.title: Queue implementation
questions.statement: Implement a queue with enqueue, dequeue, peek and size. Print values for dequeue, peek and size.
questions.input: Commands: enqueue X, dequeue, peek, size, end.
constraints: Never dequeue or peek an empty queue.

examples.input:
enqueue 4
enqueue 9
dequeue
peek
size
end
examples.explain: FIFO: dequeue removes 4, 9 is still at the front.

tests.name: mixed commands
tests.input:
enqueue 4
enqueue 9
dequeue
peek
size
end

tests.name: empty then two
tests.input:
enqueue 1
enqueue 2
size
dequeue
dequeue
end

mistakes: Using push/pop on a queue, which makes it a stack
hints: addLast/removeFirst gives FIFO order.

questions.title: Balanced parentheses
questions.statement: Check whether (), [] and {} are correctly balanced.

examples.explain: Every closing bracket must match the top of the stack.

mistakes: Forgetting to check that the stack is empty at the end
hints: Push openers; on a closer, compare with the popped top.

questions.title: Linked list implementation
questions.statement: Build a singly linked list from n values and print them in order.

examples.explain: Append each value to the tail, then traverse from the head.

mistakes: Losing the head while traversing, so the list cannot be printed again
hints: Keep a separate tail reference for O(1) appends.

questions.title: Remove linked list duplicates
questions.statement: Remove duplicate values from a linked list, keeping the first occurrence, and print the result.
questions.output: The cleaned list separated by spaces.

examples.explain: A set tracks seen values while walking the list.

mistakes: Removing the head node without updating the head reference
hints: Filter while building instead of unlinking nodes.

questions.title: Middle of a linked list
questions.statement: Print the middle node's value (the second middle for an even count) using slow/fast pointers.

examples.explain: Fast moves two steps while slow moves one.

mistakes: Advancing slow twice, which lands past the middle
hints: Check fast != null && fast.next != null.

questions.title: Detect a cycle in a linked list
questions.statement: Read n values, then k. If k >= 0, link the tail to the node at index k (0-based); otherwise leave the list acyclic. Print Cycle or No cycle.
questions.input: n and k, then n integers.

examples.explain: Floyd's algorithm: fast meets slow only inside a cycle.

mistakes: Comparing values instead of node references
hints: Compare references with ==, not values.

questions.title: Word frequency with a HashMap
questions.statement: Count how often each word appears and print word=count sorted alphabetically.

examples.explain: HashMap counts, TreeMap sorts for output.

mistakes: Using == to compare words instead of equals
hints: TreeMap sorts the keys for a stable report.

questions.title: Sort objects with a Comparator
questions.statement: Read students as name and score, then print them sorted by score descending, ties by name ascending.
questions.input: n, then n lines of "name score".

examples.explain: Comparator.comparingInt(...).reversed().thenComparing(...).

mistakes: Using subtraction in a comparator, which can overflow
hints: comparingInt avoids overflow; reversed() flips the order.

questions.title: Student management system
questions.statement: Store students with id, name and marks. Print the average marks (2 decimals) and the topper's name.
questions.input: n, then n lines of "id name marks".

examples.explain: A Student class holds the data; a loop aggregates it.

mistakes: Integer division truncating the average
hints: Cast to double before dividing and format with %.2f.

questions.title: Bank account class
questions.statement: Model a bank account with deposit and withdraw. Apply the given operations and print the final balance with 2 decimals.
questions.input: Starting balance, op count, then ops "deposit X" or "withdraw X".

examples.explain: Encapsulated state only changes through methods that validate.

mistakes: Making balance public so invalid withdrawals bypass validation
hints: Validate inside withdraw, not at the call site.

questions.title: Employee inheritance
questions.statement: Employees are dev or manager; managers earn a 20% bonus. Print the total salary with 2 decimals.
questions.input: n, then n lines of "type base".

examples.explain: Polymorphic salary() gives each subclass its own rule.

mistakes: Not marking salary() as overridable or forgetting @Override
hints: Call through the Employee reference to get polymorphism.

questions.title: Custom exception
questions.statement: Validate an age. Ages below 0 throw InvalidAgeException with the age as the message; print the exception message, else "Valid age: X".
questions.output: The exception message or the valid-age line.

examples.explain: A checked custom exception carries a descriptive message.

mistakes: Catching Exception and swallowing the message
hints: Throw in a helper, catch in main where you can report it.

questions.title: File word counter
questions.statement: Write the given sentence to a temporary file, read it back and print the number of words.

examples.explain: Files.writeString then split on whitespace.

mistakes: Forgetting to close or delete the temporary file
hints: Files.readString keeps it short; delete in the same method.

questions.title: Generic min and max
questions.statement: Read n integers and print the minimum and maximum using one generic method bounded by Comparable.

examples.explain: <T extends Comparable<T>> lets one method serve any ordered type.

mistakes: Using < on T, which does not compile for a generic type
hints: compareTo returns a negative, zero or positive int.
